Extract all Alder-relevant evidence from the three immutable sources and persist it as evidence-alder.md.

Steps:
1. Use file_read (and file_list if useful) to read sources/pilot-charter.txt ([S1]), sources/weekly-observations.txt ([S2]) and sources/reviewer-note.txt ([S3]) from the workspace. Do not open any source for writing.
2. Build an evidence note covering EVERY Alder-relevant fact, including:
   - Alder's weekday request total (expected as a check: 480) and site-weeks observed (4) — cite [S2].
   - Alder's delayed acknowledgements (expected as a check: 31) and supervisor escalations (2) — cite [S2].
   - The definition of a delayed acknowledgement (elapsed acknowledgement time greater than 15 minutes, measured after routing) — cite [S2], since this defines what '31' counts.
   - The reviewer's statement that Alder has the smallest delayed-acknowledgement count and the fewest escalations — cite [S3].
   - The reviewer's recommendation to extend Alder routing practices to Brook and Cove for two weeks — cite [S3].
   - Baseline and pilot acknowledgement medians (manual 18 minutes, routed 11 minutes) and the receipt-timestamp basis of acknowledgement — cite [S1].
   - Baseline request rate (120 requests per site-week) — cite [S1] — noting it as a charter baseline, and that 120 x 4 = 480 is consistent arithmetic, labelled as derived.
   - Program window 2026-01-05 through 2026-01-30 (four operating weeks), owner Service Operations, sites Alder/Brook/Cove with the Depot trial explicitly excluded, and the routing runbook v2 change on 2026-01-12 — cite [S1].
   - Any cross-site or charter facts that bear on Alder, such as the reviewer sampling 60 records per site (180 total) and the reconciliation of those samples to the weekly totals — cite [S2] and [S3]; and the control/data-quality lines of [S2] (no missing weekday records; the log does not identify individual customers).
3. For each fact give its citation AND a short quoted or closely paraphrased source line so the coordinator can verify the number on sight. Use a table or a bulleted list with columns/fields: Fact | Value | Citation | Source line.
4. Add a 'Limitations and exclusions found in the sources' section, at minimum: weekday-only coverage with no weekend or Depot conclusion supported [S1]; the Depot trial explicitly excluded [S1]; no individual customer identification and the 15-minute measurement convention [S2]; the reviewer's caution that the pilot cannot establish weekend performance or Depot outcomes and the decision gate to repeat measurement before any wider rollout [S3]; the runbook change on 2026-01-12 occurring mid-window [S1]; the note that supervisor escalations are counted but not defined by threshold in the sources.
5. Add an 'Expected-value check' section explicitly stating whether each expected value (480 requests; 31 delayed acknowledgements) matches the source text, and flagging any mismatch prominently. Do not alter a source reading to fit an expectation.
6. Do NOT extrapolate beyond Alder's weekday pilot data; do not infer causes, weekend or Depot behaviour, or rollout outcomes.
7. Persist the finished note itself with file_write to the path evidence-alder.md (relative to the workspace) using mission_id="r2-final-professional-2026-11-16T18-47-03-020Z-3010790-research" so it registers as an artifact, then also register the same content with save_artifact name="evidence-alder.md" and the same mission_id. Read input/operations.csv in the working directory and independently compute the operations metrics from the raw integer values. Persist the result as metrics.json in the working directory. 1) Use file_list to confirm input/operations.csv exists, then file_read it. Parse its header and all data rows. Do not invent, drop, deduplicate or convert any record or unit. 2) Count data rows (excluding the header) as row_count. 3) For totals and for each team, sum the raw integers for work_orders, completed_orders, defects, planned_minutes and actual_minutes. 4) Derive completion_percent = completed_orders / work_orders × 100, rounded to exactly 2 decimals, and minutes_per_completed_order = actual_minutes / completed_orders, rounded to exactly 2 decimals. Compute both from the raw summed integers, never from rounded or averaged sub-results. Derive schedule_variance_minutes = actual_minutes − planned_minutes as an integer. 5) Write metrics.json with root keys exactly row_count, totals, teams in that order. Each totals/team object has exactly work_orders, completed_orders, defects, planned_minutes, actual_minutes, completion_percent, minutes_per_completed_order, schedule_variance_minutes in that order. teams contains exactly Atlas, Birch, Cedar in that order. Integers are JSON numbers, not strings. The two ratio fields are JSON numbers serialized with exactly two decimal places. No extra fields, comments or wrapper. 6) Before writing, compare each recomputed value against the approved reference values listed in context. If any value differs, do not silently copy the reference. Write nothing, and report the exact field, the computed value and the reference value as a blocking discrepancy.

After metrics.json exists, read input/operations.csv and metrics.json from the working directory. Write the management document operations-brief.md in the working directory. Required content: 1) A concise Executive Recommendation of a few sentences. Base it only on the dataset. For example, prioritise Cedar, which has the lowest completion (90.48%), the most defects (8 of 18) and 340 of the 455 overall schedule-variance minutes. Make no claims about causes, costs, staffing or periods outside the data. 2) Overall Findings with the exact totals: 217 of 233 work orders completed (93.13%), 18 defects, 14985 planned vs 15440 actual minutes, schedule variance +455 minutes, 71.15 minutes per completed order. 3) Per-Team Findings for Atlas, Birch and Cedar in that order. For each team give the exact completion counts and percent, defects, planned and actual minutes, schedule variance and minutes per completed order, copied exactly from metrics.json. A compact Markdown table is acceptable. 4) A Method section. It names input/operations.csv as the sole source and covers the dataset (18 rows, six weeks, three teams). It states the exact formulas: completion_percent = completed orders / work orders × 100; minutes_per_completed_order = actual minutes / completed orders; schedule_variance_minutes = actual minutes − planned minutes. It also states that ratios are computed from raw summed integers and rounded to two decimals, that minutes are reported as minutes with no unit conversion, and that no records were invented or excluded. 5) A short Scope/Limitations note stating that conclusions are limited to the supplied six-week, three-team dataset. Before writing, verify that every number in the brief matches metrics.json exactly, and spot-check the totals against the CSV. If metrics.json is missing or inconsistent with the CSV, do not write the brief, and report the discrepancy.
